reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge is separating individual player value from collaborative synergy in basketball. Standard RAPM conflates these through unconstrained linear combinations, leading to unintuitive negative estimates. Our non-negative additivity assumption addresses this by ensuring that each player's contribution is always positive, with synergy terms capturing deviations from simple summation. This yields interpretable player ratings while maintaining lineup prediction accuracy. However, the method fails when there are too few unique lineups to identify both player and synergy effects, requiring careful regularization tuning to avoid overfitting.
